blocks.heading: Why This Decision Needs Real Numbers

items.text: Every year, a large share of Indian engineering and science graduates ask some version of the same question: should I do an MS in USA, or is it not worth it anymore given the cost and the visa uncertainty.
It is not automatically a life-changing investment, and it is not automatically a scam either.
If you are earlier in the decision and still weighing whether higher studies makes sense at all right now, read first job vs higher studies India before you shortlist universities.

blocks.heading: MS in USA Vs Staying in India

items.text: Your field (commonly computer science, data science, certain engineering specializations) has strong, verifiable US employer demand at the OPT stage, not just at the H1B stage.
You can fund most of the cost through savings, assistantships, or scholarships, keeping loan exposure to an amount your family can absorb even in a no-H1B outcome.
You have already checked that the specific university and program you are targeting places graduates into roles that match the earning ranges above, not just a general "top ranked" reputation.

You have a real answer for what you do professionally if you return to India after OPT, the US degree and work experience still needs to translate into a stronger India-based role, not just a stronger visa story.
